origin.description: Tests whether every eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix is larger than the tolerance.

arguments.name: tol
arguments.text: Eigenvalues must exceed tol. The default follows the matrix size and the largest absolute eigenvalue.

arguments.name: method
arguments.text: eigen, the default, or chol. A unique prefix is enough.

origin.details: On this R, a successful chol() has class matrix and array. The comparison with try-error then has length 2, so method chol raises when the factor exists and returns false when it does not. Python raises the same error text.
origin.value: True or false on the eigenvalue path.
origin.example:
bad <- matrix(c(1, 2, 2, 1), 2)
msg <- tryCatch(is.positive.definite(M, method='chol'), error=function(e) conditionMessage(e))
c(as.integer(is.positive.definite(M)), as.integer(is.positive.definite(bad, method='chol')), nchar(msg))

translation.description: Tests whether every eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix is larger than the tolerance.

arguments.name: tol
arguments.text: Eigenvalues must exceed tol. The default follows the matrix size and the largest absolute eigenvalue.

arguments.name: method
arguments.text: eigen, the default, or chol. A unique prefix is enough.

translation.details: On this R, a successful chol() has class matrix and array. The comparison with try-error then has length 2, so method chol raises when the factor exists and returns false when it does not. Python raises the same error text.
translation.value: True or false on the eigenvalue path.
translation.example:
from corpcor import is_positive_definite
bad = np.array([[1.0, 2.0],[2.0, 1.0]])
try:
    is_positive_definite(M, method='chol')
    msg = ''
except ValueError as exc:
    msg = str(exc)
return [int(is_positive_definite(M)), int(is_positive_definite(bad, method='chol')), len(msg)]
